title: DeLiBA-K: Speeding-up Hardware-Accelerated Distributed Storage Access by Tighter Linux Kernel Integration and Use of a Modern API
problem: User-space interactions in DeLiBA-1 and -2 introduce overhead when accessing hardware-accelerated distributed storage. DeLiBA-K addresses this by operating at the Linux kernel level to reduce latency and improve I/O parallelism.
motivation: Efficient hardware-accelerated I/O is critical for improving performance in data-intensive enterprise applications and large-scale distributed systems.
method: DeLiBA-K operates at the Linux kernel level instead of as a user-space program, eliminating the overhead of context switching—the repeated transitions between user space (where programs run) and kernel space (where the OS manages hardware). It uses io_uring (an asynchronous I/O API that issues multiple requests in parallel rather than sequentially) to communicate directly with the block and network I/O stacks. This runs on a 16nm AMD Alveo U280 FPGA, a programmable hardware accelerator. The result is reduced latency and improved I/O parallelism by avoiding context-switching overhead.
key_novelty: The core innovation is implementing io_uring inside the Linux kernel instead of user space, eliminating context-switching overhead when applications access FPGA-accelerated storage.
contributions: Kernel-level reimplementation of DeLiBA framework bypassing user-space interactions
Integration of io_uring Asynchronous I/O API with AMD Alveo U280 FPGA framework
